comparison: Strong agreement on basic characterization findings (C2-C10, C18, C84). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by calcium imaging data. OpenEval includes additional claims (C13, C14) about running modulation that peer reviewers address separately in R2.

Both address running modulation claims (C15-C17) and find them supported. OpenEval groups these with additional claims (C11-C12, C85-C86) about comparisons to V1, while peer reviewers focus specifically on the differential modulation patterns between ACx and V1.

Disagreement on AM mismatch responses (C19-C25, C87). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by experimental data, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN due to concerns about whether responses reflect true prediction errors versus simpler sound offset sensitivity.

Agreement on properties of AM mismatch neurons (C29-C30, C33-C35, C90). Both evaluations find these claims supported. OpenEval's result covers broader set of AM mismatch claims while peer result focuses on neuron properties and V1 parallels.

Agreement on closed vs. open loop differences (C26-C27). Both find these claims supported. Peer reviewers note initial concerns about velocity correlations that were addressed, while OpenEval emphasizes this as a clear negative result with appropriate controls.

Partial overlap on AM mismatch properties (C36-C38, C40-C41). Both evaluations support these specific claims about closed/open loop differences, though they are grouped differently with other claims in each evaluation.

Perfect agreement on lack of VM mismatch responses (C44-C54). Both evaluations find these claims supported, accepting the negative result at population level in ACx as well-controlled and clearly demonstrated.

Strong agreement on multimodal interaction findings (C55-C63, C114, C118). Both evaluations strongly support these claims about super-additive responses and non-linear integration. Peer reviewers describe this as 'compelling evidence' while OpenEval emphasizes the magnitude and selective populations.

Disagreement on theoretical generalizations (C42-C43, C112-C113, C116-C117). OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN as extending beyond current data, while peer reviewers rate them SUPPORTED, strongly endorsing the non-hierarchical interaction conclusions. Peer reviewers find the evidence 'compelling' while OpenEval sees them as reasonable but requiring additional evidence.

Agreement on ACx vs V1 differences (C93-C97). Both evaluations find the observations supported but acknowledge the explanations are speculative. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenging the speculative nature.
Perfect agreement on sampling bias interpretation (C31-C32). Both evaluations find these claims supported based on prior work and recording approach. Neither evaluation challenges this reasoning.

Agreement on calcium imaging limitations and inferences (C98-C100). Both evaluations support these claims despite acknowledged methodological limitations. Both find the magnitude of effects and selective populations sufficient to justify conclusions about non-linear interactions.

Agreement on mechanistic speculations (C101-C111). Both evaluations rate these UNCERTAIN, acknowledging they are hypotheses requiring future validation. Peer reviewers note circuit mechanisms 'are still unclear and will require further investigation' while OpenEval emphasizes these are logical but not directly tested.

Partial overlap on sustained response interpretation (C39). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN as speculative and not directly tested. Peer result R5 addresses broader theoretical claims but includes C39; peer reviewers appear to accept this interpretation as part of their SUPPORTED rating for the broader predictive processing framework.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims (C119-C123) as SUPPORTED factual descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are straightforward methodological details not typically challenged in peer review.

OpenEval evaluates background/citation claims (C1, C65-C83, C88-C89, C124-C125) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers typically do not separately evaluate background literature claims.
OpenEval evaluates limitation acknowledgment (C115) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers implicitly agree by noting circuit mechanisms remain unclear.
